READING

**Step 1 – Strip the Vantwyn seasons to their net contribution**

Per season:
- Pollination fee: 400 × £168 = **£67,200**
- Haulage and labour: **–£6,900**
- Spray colony losses: 9 % × 400 = 36 colonies × £210 = **–£7,560**
- Borage foregone (colonies out too late for Kirkhallow): 400 × £71 = **–£28,400**
- Net per season: **£24,340**

Over three seasons: £24,340 × 3 = **£73,020**

Add the residual kit value in 2030 as stated under TREVANNOCK: **£20,000**

TREVANNOCK total realised value over the contract period: **£93,020**

**Step 2 – State ORMSCLEUCH's equivalent**

Sell to Ravensgate now: **£96,000**, received in full before the offer closes (28 November 2026, after the Vantwyn decision deadline of 31 October).

**Step 3 – Head-to-head at zero discount rate**

| | TREVANNOCK | ORMSCLEUCH |
|---|---|---|
| Equipment proceeds | £20,000 (2030) | £96,000 (2026) |
| Net Vantwyn income | £73,020 | £0 |
| Borage maintained | lost (£85,200) | fully earned |
| **Total (kit + pollination net)** | **£93,020** | **£96,000** |

ORMSCLEUCH is already ahead by **£2,980 on undiscounted cash** — the simplest, most favourable possible test for TREVANNOCK. Every real-world adjustment widens that gap:

**Step 4 – Time value**
£96,000 lands in late 2026. The TREVANNOCK cash arrives in three annual tranches of £24,340 (2027–2029) plus £20,000 in early 2030. Even at 5 % the NPV of those TREVANNOCK receipts is roughly £83,300, putting ORMSCLEUCH ahead by around **£12,700** in present value.

**Step 5 – The 9 % spray-loss figure is a single data point and is not conservative**
The 9 % is Whinnerdale Bees' experience with a single grower on the same programme — one observation with unknown variance. Vantwyn will not vary their spray schedule. If losses ran to, say, 13 %: 52 × £210 = £10,920/season, adding another **£10,080** of cost over three seasons. The replacement-colony cost also absorbs queen-rearing shed capacity. TREVANNOCK carries meaningful downside risk that ORMSCLEUCH does not.

**Step 6 – The Coldharbour and Nyefield opportunity under TREVANNOCK**
With 400 colonies committed to Vantwyn from April, only 240 remain for anything else. That is too few to run a meaningful second pollination contract without a substantial colony-building programme. The opportunity is real but structurally constrained. It cannot rescue the arithmetic even if it materialised at Vantwyn rates, because the kit has essentially no capacity headroom and the lorry loses its vale permit at the end of 2029 anyway.

**Step 7 – Sunk costs and the 2024 investment**
The £187,000 spent in 2024 is sunk; the question is forward value only. The Ravensgate offer already prices the pallets and lorry at £96,000 — the queen rearing shed is not part of that offer and retains option value, or can be disposed of separately. Keeping the kit to justify past expenditure would be a classic sunk-cost error.

**Step 8 – Strategic fit**
Three pollination contracts lapsed in 2025 with none renewed. The migratory side has sat idle for a full season. ORMSCLEUCH converts a depreciating, idle asset into immediate capital, removes a concurrent operational complexity, and refocuses entirely on the 640-colony honey business that generated £143,000 last season on zero additional haulage. That business needs no lorry permit, no spray-risk management, and no reliance on growers who will not vary their programmes.

**Step 9 – Decision**
ORMSCLEUCH is ahead in cash at zero discount, materially ahead in present value, and carries none of the spray-loss variance risk. TREVANNOCK would need the three seasons to outperform expectations and the Coldharbour/Nyefield leads to crystallise into full-rate contracts with spare colony capacity — a chain of positive assumptions against a business where the existing contracts have already lapsed.

---

READING
  The Vantwyn seasons net £73,020 across three years; the residual kit value in 2030 is £20,000; combined that is £93,020 against £96,000 available now from Ravensgate. At zero discount rate ORMSCLEUCH is already £2,980 ahead. Accounting for time value (£96,000 received in 2026 vs income spread to 2030) widens the gap to roughly £12,700 in present-value terms. The 9 % spray-loss figure rests on a single beekeeper's experience with no stated variance, and Vantwyn's refusal to vary their programme removes any mitigation route. With 400 colonies tied to Vantwyn, only 240 remain for additional pollination work, so the Coldharbour and Nyefield leads cannot rescue the return on the kit even if they contracted at Vantwyn rates. Three contracts lapsed in 2025 with no renewals, the migratory side has been idle for a full season, and the lorry loses its vale permit at the end of 2029 in any case. ORMSCLEUCH turns an asset that is both depreciating and idle into immediate capital, preserves the full 640-colony honey yield, and removes operational and agrochemical risk at a cost that is negative on every measure tested.

CALL
  ORMSCLEUCH

GROUNDS
  Even at zero discount rate the Ravensgate proceeds (£96,000 now) exceed three seasons of Vantwyn net income plus the 2030 kit residual (£93,020), and every further adjustment — time value, spray-loss variance, the lorry's permit expiry, and the structural constraint that 400 colonies at Vantwyn leave no room for the Coldharbour and Nyefield leads — widens that margin in ORMSCLEUCH's favour.
